KEY MESSAGE 1: A Heat Advisory is in effect for the coastal 
counties this afternoon as hot and humid conditions make a return. 
Additional Heat Advisories will likely be required through the week 
and into the weekend. Extreme Heat Watches/Warnings cannot be ruled 
out, especially towards the end of the week.

Heat headlines are likely into the weekend as heat index values soar 
into the 100-110 range each afternoon through mid-week and upwards 
of 115 late in the week. The daily record highs and record high 
minimum temperatures will likely be challenged at our three climate 
sites (see Climate Section for more details). Given the very mild 
overnight periods and minimal coverage of precipitation, there will 
be few instances of relief from the heat this week and into the 
weekend. 

Today and Wednesday: Ridging aloft will dominate over the 
southeastern states today and Wednesday, with high temperatures each 
day reaching into the mid 90s. Dew points will surge behind the sea 
breeze, likely reaching values in the mid to upper 70s. This will 
yield heat index values as high as 110 generally east of I-95. A 
Heat Advisory is in effect for the coastal counties today from 11 AM 
to 8 PM. Another Heat Advisory will likely be required for the same 
locations on Wednesday. 

Thursday and Friday: The ridging aloft amplifies towards the end of 
the week, likely bringing the warmest temperatures of the heat wave. 
Highs on each day will likely reach into the upper 90s, with a brief 
moment of touching 100 not out of the question. Heat index values 
west of I-95 will likely reach 105-108 (Heat Advisory) with 
locations east of I-95 reaching heat index values as high as 115. 
Extreme Heat Watches/Warnings may be required for these locations.  

This Weekend: The center of ridging aloft will shift slightly 
westward, resulting in a slight downtick of temperatures. However, 
heat index values are still forecast to reach upwards of 110 along 
the coastal corridor likely necessitating additional Heat 
Advisories.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms will develop 
across southeast Georgia and the lower South Carolina Lowcountry, 
especially near the coast. A few storms may produce damaging wind 
gusts and heavy downpours this afternoon and evening. Additional 
severe thunderstorms are possible across portions of the region late 
Wednesday.

Tuesday: A sfc trough should remain across the central Carolinas 
into GA through this evening. Satellite water vapor shows an MCV 
over the middle AL/GA this morning, expected to ripple over SE GA 
this afternoon. In addition, the sfc trough to the west should draw 
the sea breeze inland this afternoon. Recent run of the HREF 
indicates that deep convection may begin to develop ahead of the 
MCV, likely forming several cool pools. Hot and humid conditions 
across the forecast area will likely yield SBCAPE values between 
2500-3000 J/kg. In addition, forecast soundings indicate DCAPE 
values between 1000-1500 J/kg. Given the expansive field of DCAPE, 
the cool pools should travel long distances, potentially interacting 
with the sea breeze. This interaction should develop scattered to 
numerous thunderstorms along the coast, especially between Chatham 
and Charleston counties. The environment featuring moderate 
instability and DCAPE along with effective bulk shear around 20 kts 
may support a few severe thunderstorms, producing damaging wind 
gusts. The severe potential appears the greatest across Chatham, 
Jasper, Beaufort, and Colleton counties this afternoon. In fact, 0Z 
GEFS indicates that most of the forecast has a 5-15% neighborhood 
prob of damaging winds, with in excess of 15% near the mouth of the 
Savannah River. In addition to the severe risk, multicell storms may 
produce localize areas of heavy rainfall, with some locations 
receiving in excess of 3 inches. If a swath of heavy rain occurs 
over a coastal city, then Flash Flooding may occur.

Wednesday: The center of 595 DM ridge is forecast to slide west over 
the northern Gulf. As a result, NW to SE heights may align over the 
forecast area. NAM12 and CAMS indicate that at least isolated storms 
may develop over portions of SE GA Wednesday afternoon. 
Interestingly, the NAM12 and GFS shows an MCS tracking from the 
Upstate to the Coastal Plain Wed evening. Given the mid-level 
heights and lingering elevated instability, the potential for an MCS 
reaching the forecast appears high enough to increase PoPs Wednesday 
evening and overnight to at least SCHC. SPC has highlighted this 
potential severe weather with a Marginal Risk.
